$\therefore AB=AD$,\\
Since $\angle BAD=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ABD$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore \angle BAD=\angle ABD=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle DBC=\angle BDF=\angle C=60^\circ$,\\
In $\triangle CDE$ and $\triangle DBF$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}CD=DB\\ \angle C=\angle BDF\\ CE=DF\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore \triangle CDE \cong \triangle DBF\left(SAS\right)$,\\
$\therefore \angle CDE=\angle DBF$,\\
$\therefore \angle GBE=\angle BDE$,\\
$\therefore \angle DBF+\angle GBE=\angle DBF+\angle BDE=\angle BGE=\angle DGF=60^\circ=\angle BAD$,\\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral $ABGD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral,\\
$\therefore \angle BGD=120^\circ$,\\
As shown in the figure, draw $AM\perp DE$ and $AN\perp BF$ from point $A$, with the feet $M$ and $N$ respectively,\\
Since $AG$ bisects $\angle BGD$,\\
$\therefore AN=AM$,\\
In $Rt\triangle ABN$ and $Rt\triangle ADM$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}AB=AD\\ AN=AM\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore Rt\triangle ABN \cong Rt\triangle ADM\left(HL\right)$,\\
$\therefore BN=DM$,\\
$\therefore GN+GM=BG+DG=3+5=8$,\\

$\left\{\begin{array}{l}AG=AG\\ AN=AM\end{array}\right.$,\\
